newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: CHILUBA WINS LANDSLIDE IN DISPUTED ZAMBIAN POLL.
newsitem.headline: CHILUBA WINS LANDSLIDE IN DISPUTED ZAMBIAN POLL.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba seemed headed for a landslide victory on Wednesday as vote-counting passed the halfway mark in the southern African country's disputed general election.
Chiluba had secured 76 percent of the votes cast in 87 of 150 constituencies reporting final results, according to the latest figures released by the elections office.

Chiluba was leading with 600,965 of the 786,583 votes counted by mid-afternoon -- enough to give him at least 50 percent of the overall 1.1 million votes cast in Monday's polling even before results from 63 remaining constituencies were counted.
His closest rival, Zambia Democratic Congress leader Dean Mungomba, trailed with 94,237 votes.
Seven opposition parties boycotted the poll, charging that Chiluba had rigged the campaign in advance and said they would not recongise the result.

Two groups monitoring the election, however, gave conflicting views of the voting. A Zambian groups said the election was neither free nor fair since half of eligible voters were unfairly excluded but an international group said it found the ballotting generally correct.
